bull.b: Rapid FILSPARI growth across IgA nephropathy and FSGS demonstrates expanding patient adoption and commercial execution. Continued uptake can broaden the revenue base, improve operating leverage, and support Travere’s ability to fund development of additional rare-disease therapies.

bull.t: High Gross Profitability and Improving Cash Flow
bull.b: The combination of very high gross profitability and positive operating cash flow indicates that product sales are beginning to support the business economically. If sustained, this provides greater internal funding capacity for commercialization and pipeline investment while reducing dependence on external financing.

Extended U.S. method-of-use patent protection can help preserve FILSPARI’s commercial position in FSGS and support longer-term revenue durability. Protection through 2037 also gives Travere additional time to build adoption, strengthen prescriber familiarity, and monetize its clinical evidence.

bear.b: The sharply increased debt burden and thin equity base leave limited financial cushion if operating performance weakens. High leverage can constrain capital allocation, increase refinancing exposure, and make it more difficult to absorb setbacks in FILSPARI adoption or pipeline development.

bear.t: Bottom-Line Losses and Modest Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Although revenue and operating cash flow have improved, Travere has not yet converted scale into durable GAAP profitability, and free cash flow remains modest. Ongoing losses limit internally generated capital, particularly while the company carries substantial debt and funds clinical programs.

Higher discounts reduce the revenue retained from each FILSPARI prescription and may pressure future net sales growth as FSGS becomes a larger mix. Competition in IgA nephropathy and the need for physician and payer education could further increase the effort required to sustain adoption.
